evidence_quote:
The number of jumps required to reach 80% full is:
   \[
   \frac{1,600,000 \text{ ml}}{400 \text{ ml/jump}} = 4,000 \text{ jumps}
   \]
question_evidence_quote: Jim has to get everyone out of the pool, clean, and refill it when it gets below 80% full.
observed_error: The response divides the water remaining at 80% capacity by the water lost per jump.
violated_condition: Jumps to reach 80% full equal the loss from full capacity to 80% capacity divided by 400 ml per jump.
error_description: The response uses 1,600,000 ml, the water remaining at 80% full, as the amount splashed out when calculating jumps. It should use the decrease from full capacity to that level. The division is executed correctly, but its numerator represents the wrong quantity.
